paragraphs.title: The Opening of Moses’ Speech in the Wilderness

easy.question: Who spoke to the Israelites according to these verses?
answers: Moses
Joshua
Aaron
easy.explanation: The verse says, “These are the words which Moses spoke to all Israel.”

easy.question: To whom did Moses speak?
answers: The kings of the nations
All Israel
The tribe of Levi alone
easy.explanation: The verses state that Moses spoke to all Israel and to the children of Israel.

easy.question: Where did Moses speak to Israel?
answers: At Mount Sinai
In Jerusalem
Across the Jordan, in the land of Moab
easy.explanation: Verse 5 says that Moses spoke across the Jordan in the land of Moab.

medium.question: What happened before Moses began explaining the law?
answers: The Israelites reached the Red Sea
Moses defeated Sihon and Og
The people left Egypt
medium.explanation: Verse 5 describes Moses explaining the law after defeating Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan.

medium.question: What does the phrase “began to declare” mean in this context?
answers: He became tired
He hid himself
He began or agreed to undertake something
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Moses began explaining the law.

medium.question: When did Moses speak to the Israelites?
answers: In the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day
In the first year, in the first month
In the thirtieth year, in the third month
medium.explanation: Verse 3 gives the exact time: the fortieth year, the eleventh month, and the first day of the month.

challenge.question: What contrast can be seen by comparing verses 2 and 3?
answers: The journey was longer than expected
The journey began after entering the land
An eleven-day journey was connected with events that lasted until the fortieth year
challenge.explanation: Verse 2 mentions an eleven-day journey, while verse 3 describes events in the fortieth year, highlighting the contrast between distance and time.

challenge.question: Which pairing of king and location is correct?
answers: Sihon at Heshbon and Og at Astaroth in Edrei
Sihon in Bashan and Og at Heshbon
Sihon at Edrei and Og in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: Sihon is described as the Amorite king who lived at Heshbon, and Og as the king of Bashan who lived at Astaroth in Edrei.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the repetition of “across the Jordan” in verses 1 and 5?
answers: Moses spoke inside Egypt
The speech was given east of the Jordan, before entering the land
The people had already settled in Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The phrase identifies the speech’s location across the Jordan, in the land of Moab, before Israel entered the land.

questions.question: What contrast can be seen by comparing verses 2 and 3?
answers: The journey was longer than expected
The journey began after entering the land
An eleven-day journey was connected with events that lasted until the fortieth year
questions.explanation: Verse 2 mentions an eleven-day journey, while verse 3 describes events in the fortieth year, highlighting the contrast between distance and time.

questions.question: Which pairing of king and location is correct?
answers: Sihon at Heshbon and Og at Astaroth in Edrei
Sihon in Bashan and Og at Heshbon
Sihon at Edrei and Og in the wilderness
questions.explanation: Sihon is described as the Amorite king who lived at Heshbon, and Og as the king of Bashan who lived at Astaroth in Edrei.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the repetition of “across the Jordan” in verses 1 and 5?
answers: Moses spoke inside Egypt
The speech was given east of the Jordan, before entering the land
The people had already settled in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: The phrase identifies the speech’s location across the Jordan, in the land of Moab, before Israel entered the land.

paragraphs.title: The Command to Leave and Possess the Land

easy.question: Where did the Lord speak to the Israelites?
answers: At Horeb
In Jerusalem
In Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord spoke to them at Horeb.

easy.question: What did the Lord command the Israelites to do?
answers: Remain at the mountain
Turn and set out
Return to Egypt
easy.explanation: The Lord told them, “Turn and take your journey.”

easy.question: What did the Lord set before the Israelites?
answers: The land
The sea
The wilderness
easy.explanation: The verse says, “I have set the land before you.”

medium.question: What does “You have dwelt long enough” mean in this context?
answers: It was time to stop staying there
You have a large mountain
You must build more houses
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the Israelites had stayed at the mountain long enough and should continue their journey.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in these verses?
answers: Receiving the land, staying at the mountain, then the Lord speaks
The Lord speaks, they travel toward the land, and they possess it
Possessing the land, traveling, then the Lord speaks
medium.explanation: First the Lord speaks at Horeb, then commands them to travel, and finally commands them to enter and possess the land.

medium.question: Why did the Lord command the Israelites to leave the mountain?
answers: They had to advance toward the land promised to them
The mountain belonged to other nations
They had to return to Egypt
medium.explanation: Leaving was part of advancing toward the land that the Lord swore to give to the patriarchs and their descendants.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the command “Go in and possess the land”?
answers: The land had already been given to them without any action
They had to act in order to receive the promised land
They only needed to view the land from a distance
challenge.explanation: The Lord set the land before them, but commanded them to enter and possess it—to act in order to take hold of it.

challenge.question: What special detail does verse 8 give about the promise of the land?
answers: The promise was given only to Moses
The promise was given to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and to their descendants
The promise was given only to the generation that left Egypt
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly mentions the three patriarchs and their descendants.

challenge.question: What does the list of regions in verse 7 show about the extent of the land?
answers: The command concerned only a small area around the mountain
The land included various broad regions extending to the Euphrates
The people were to travel only along the seacoast
challenge.explanation: The verse lists varied regions—including the plain, hills, valleys, the south, and the seacoast—and extends the boundary to the Euphrates.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the command “Go in and possess the land”?
answers: The land had already been given to them without any action
They had to act in order to receive the promised land
They only needed to view the land from a distance
questions.explanation: The Lord set the land before them, but commanded them to enter and possess it—to act in order to take hold of it.

questions.question: What special detail does verse 8 give about the promise of the land?
answers: The promise was given only to Moses
The promise was given to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and to their descendants
The promise was given only to the generation that left Egypt
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly mentions the three patriarchs and their descendants.

questions.question: What does the list of regions in verse 7 show about the extent of the land?
answers: The command concerned only a small area around the mountain
The land included various broad regions extending to the Euphrates
The people were to travel only along the seacoast
questions.explanation: The verse lists varied regions—including the plain, hills, valleys, the south, and the seacoast—and extends the boundary to the Euphrates.

paragraphs.title: The Growth of the People and the Establishment of Leadership

easy.question: Why did Moses say, “I am not able to bear you myself alone”?
answers: It was too difficult for him to bear the people’s burdens alone
The people refused to listen to him
They had no leaders at all
easy.explanation: Moses said he could not bear the people’s burden, responsibilities, and disputes alone.

easy.question: What were the Israelites compared to in verse 10?
answers: The sand of the sea
The stars of heaven
The trees of the forest
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Israelites were as numerous as the stars of heaven.

easy.question: Whom did Moses appoint to lead the people?
answers: All the Israelites
The priests alone
Tribal leaders and wise, respected men
easy.explanation: Moses took tribal leaders and wise, respected men and appointed them as leaders.

medium.question: What happened after the Israelites said, “The thing which you have spoken is good for us to do”?
answers: Moses selected suitable men and appointed them as leaders
The Israelites immediately began a new journey
Moses withdrew his proposal
medium.explanation: After the people agreed, Moses took tribal leaders and wise men and gave them leadership roles.

medium.question: What does “your cumbrance” mean in the phrase “your cumbrance, and your burden, and your strife”?
answers: Your joy
The trouble and difficulty connected with you
Your journeys in the wilderness
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the trouble and burden involved in caring for and governing the people.

medium.question: Why did Moses propose appointing additional leaders?
answers: He wanted to stop speaking with the people
The people were too small to govern
The growth of the people made it difficult for Moses to handle everything alone
medium.explanation: The people had greatly increased, so Moses needed others to help carry the responsibility.

challenge.question: What does the division into captains of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens show?
answers: There was an organized, tiered leadership system
All the leaders belonged to one family
Leaders were chosen only according to age
challenge.explanation: The divisions into different group sizes show an organized hierarchy for governing the people.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Moses’ request for men “among your tribes”?
answers: Leaders were chosen only from the tribe of Levi
Each tribe had its own representatives and leaders
All the tribes left the camp
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that leadership was organized according to the tribes.

challenge.question: What is the connection between the blessing of growth in verses 10–11 and appointing leaders in verses 13–15?
answers: As the people multiplied, a broader leadership system was needed
As the people multiplied, Moses dismissed all the leaders
The growth caused the people to stop making decisions
challenge.explanation: The people’s great growth was a blessing, but it also created a greater burden, requiring many organized leaders.

questions.question: What does the division into captains of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens show?
answers: There was an organized, tiered leadership system
All the leaders belonged to one family
Leaders were chosen only according to age
questions.explanation: The divisions into different group sizes show an organized hierarchy for governing the people.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Moses’ request for men “among your tribes”?
answers: Leaders were chosen only from the tribe of Levi
Each tribe had its own representatives and leaders
All the tribes left the camp
questions.explanation: The phrase shows that leadership was organized according to the tribes.

questions.question: What is the connection between the blessing of growth in verses 10–11 and appointing leaders in verses 13–15?
answers: As the people multiplied, a broader leadership system was needed
As the people multiplied, Moses dismissed all the leaders
The growth caused the people to stop making decisions
questions.explanation: The people’s great growth was a blessing, but it also created a greater burden, requiring many organized leaders.

paragraphs.title: Just Judgment for All the People

easy.question: Whom did Moses command to judge justly?
answers: The judges
The kings
The priests
easy.explanation: Moses addressed this command to the judges.

easy.question: Between whom were the judges to judge justly?
answers: Between a king and his servant
Between a man, his brother, and the stranger with him
Between a priest and a Levite
easy.explanation: The verse refers to judgment between a man and his brother and the stranger with him.

easy.question: Whom were the judges to hear in court?
answers: Only the important person
Only the older person
The small as well as the great
easy.explanation: The verse says, “You shall hear the small as well as the great.”

medium.question: Why were the judges forbidden to fear anyone in judgment?
answers: Because judgment belongs to God
Because witnesses need not be heard
Because only the weak matter in court
medium.explanation: The verse says, “Do not be afraid of anyone, for the judgment is God’s.”

medium.question: What does “you shall not be afraid of the face of man” mean in this context?
answers: You must not write anything
You must not fear or be intimidated by a person
You must not invite anyone
medium.explanation: The context means that judges must not fear or be intimidated by anyone during a trial.

medium.question: What should be done when a matter is too difficult for the judges?
answers: Ignore it
Decide according to the person’s wealth
Bring it to Moses
medium.explanation: Moses says, “The cause that is too hard for you, bring it unto me, and I will hear it.”

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the mention of the stranger in the laws of judgment?
answers: Even a non-Israelite had the right to fair judgment
A stranger could not be judged
The stranger judged the whole people
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly includes the stranger, showing that he too was included in the protection of justice.

challenge.question: What does “you shall not respect persons” mean in a legal context?
answers: Judges may not look at people
Judges may not favor someone because of status or connections
Judges may not identify the parties
challenge.explanation: The phrase requires judges to be impartial and not favor one party.

challenge.question: What does “you shall hear the small as well as the great” teach about justice?
answers: Only important people may speak
The small are always right
Every side must be given an opportunity to be heard
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes equal consideration, regardless of age, status, or importance.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the mention of the stranger in the laws of judgment?
answers: Even a non-Israelite had the right to fair judgment
A stranger could not be judged
The stranger judged the whole people
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly includes the stranger, showing that he too was included in the protection of justice.

questions.question: What does “you shall not respect persons” mean in a legal context?
answers: Judges may not look at people
Judges may not favor someone because of status or connections
Judges may not identify the parties
questions.explanation: The phrase requires judges to be impartial and not favor one party.

questions.question: What does “you shall hear the small as well as the great” teach about justice?
answers: Only important people may speak
The small are always right
Every side must be given an opportunity to be heard
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes equal consideration, regardless of age, status, or importance.

paragraphs.title: The Journey from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea

easy.question: From where did the Israelites travel at the beginning of this passage?
answers: Kadesh-barnea
Horeb
Mount Seir
easy.explanation: Verse 19 says, “When we departed from Horeb.”

easy.question: What did the Lord give Israel according to these verses?
answers: The wilderness
Mount Horeb
The land
easy.explanation: Verse 21 says that the Lord set the land before them.

easy.question: What did Moses tell the people not to fear?
answers: Entering the land
The great wilderness
Leaving Horeb
easy.explanation: Moses commanded them not to fear or be discouraged as they entered the land.

medium.question: What happened after the Israelites reached Kadesh-barnea?
answers: Moses said they had reached the mountain of the Amorites
They immediately returned to Horeb
They remained in the wilderness
medium.explanation: After reaching Kadesh-barnea, Moses said they had come to the mountain of the Amorites, which the Lord was giving them.

medium.question: What does “terrible” mean in “that great and terrible wilderness”?
answers: A small wilderness
A wilderness that inspires fear
A wilderness full of joy
medium.explanation: Here “terrible” means frightening or awe-inspiring; the wilderness was described as vast and frightening.

medium.question: Why did Moses encourage the people to go up and possess the land?
answers: The wilderness was already inhabited
The people wanted to leave Horeb
The Lord had given them the land and kept His promise
medium.explanation: Moses explained that the Lord was giving them the land as He had promised their fathers.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the command “Go up and possess it,” even though the Lord had already given the land?
answers: The people had to act in order to receive the land in practice
The Lord did not intend to give them the land
The people had to remain outside the land
challenge.explanation: The verse connects the Lord’s gift with the people’s need to go up, act, and possess the land.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the journey took place under divine command?
answers: The wilderness was called great and terrible
It says they traveled as the Lord commanded
They reached Kadesh-barnea
challenge.explanation: Verse 19 explicitly says they traveled through the wilderness as the Lord commanded.

challenge.question: What does “Fear not, neither be discouraged” mean in the context of entering the land?
answers: The people should return to the wilderness
The people could ignore the Lord’s words
The people had to overcome both fear and discouragement
challenge.explanation: The two expressions encourage the people not to fear or shrink back from the task.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the command “Go up and possess it,” even though the Lord had already given the land?
answers: The people had to act in order to receive the land in practice
The Lord did not intend to give them the land
The people had to remain outside the land
questions.explanation: The verse connects the Lord’s gift with the people’s need to go up, act, and possess the land.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the journey took place under divine command?
answers: The wilderness was called great and terrible
It says they traveled as the Lord commanded
They reached Kadesh-barnea
questions.explanation: Verse 19 explicitly says they traveled through the wilderness as the Lord commanded.

questions.question: What does “Fear not, neither be discouraged” mean in the context of entering the land?
answers: The people should return to the wilderness
The people could ignore the Lord’s words
The people had to overcome both fear and discouragement
questions.explanation: The two expressions encourage the people not to fear or shrink back from the task.

paragraphs.title: The Sending of the Twelve Spies

easy.question: Who asked to send men ahead of the Israelites?
answers: The Israelites
Moses alone
The king of Egypt
easy.explanation: The Israelites approached Moses and asked to send men ahead of them.

easy.question: How many men were chosen to search out the land?
answers: Twelve from every tribe
Twelve men altogether
Seventy men
easy.explanation: Moses took twelve men, one from each tribe.

easy.question: What did the men bring from the land?
answers: Water from a well
Stones from the mountain
Fruit from the land
easy.explanation: The verse says they took fruit from the land in their hands.

medium.question: What did Moses do after the proposal pleased him?
answers: He chose twelve men, one from each tribe
He sent the entire people into the land
He built cities in the land
medium.explanation: After agreeing to the proposal, Moses chose twelve men, one from each tribe.

medium.question: What does “search us out the land” mean in this context?
answers: Dig holes in the ground
Inspect and investigate the land
Guard the land
medium.explanation: In the context of sending men ahead, it means to inspect and investigate the land, the route, and its cities.

medium.question: Why did the Israelites ask to send men into the land?
answers: To find water in the wilderness
To choose a new king
To learn the route and the cities they would enter
medium.explanation: They wanted the men to report the route and the cities to which they would go.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “one of a tribe”?
answers: Each tribe was represented by one man
Each tribe sent twelve men
Only one tribe took part in the mission
challenge.explanation: The phrase means that one representative was chosen from each of the twelve tribes.

challenge.question: What do the spies emphasize by saying, “It is a good land which the Lord our God gives us”?
answers: The land belonged only to the spies
The land was a gift that the Lord was giving the people
The land was unfit for settlement
challenge.explanation: The words “gives us” present the land as a gift from the Lord to Israel.

challenge.question: Which detail supports the men’s report that the land was good?
answers: They stayed there for many years
They said they saw no cities
They brought fruit from the land
challenge.explanation: Bringing actual fruit from the land served as evidence that it was fertile and good.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “one of a tribe”?
answers: Each tribe was represented by one man
Each tribe sent twelve men
Only one tribe took part in the mission
questions.explanation: The phrase means that one representative was chosen from each of the twelve tribes.

questions.question: What do the spies emphasize by saying, “It is a good land which the Lord our God gives us”?
answers: The land belonged only to the spies
The land was a gift that the Lord was giving the people
The land was unfit for settlement
questions.explanation: The words “gives us” present the land as a gift from the Lord to Israel.

questions.question: Which detail supports the men’s report that the land was good?
answers: They stayed there for many years
They said they saw no cities
They brought fruit from the land
questions.explanation: Bringing actual fruit from the land served as evidence that it was fertile and good.

paragraphs.title: The People’s Refusal and Fear of the Enemy

easy.question: What did the Israelites refuse to do?
answers: Go up into the land
Return to Egypt
Build cities
easy.explanation: The verse says, “You would not go up.”

easy.question: What did the Israelites claim about the Lord?
answers: He had forgotten them
He hated them
He was afraid of them
easy.explanation: They said, “Because the Lord hated us, he brought us out of Egypt.”

easy.question: What did the Israelites fear in the land?
answers: A lack of water
War between the tribes
The large people and the fortified cities
easy.explanation: They said the people were greater and taller, the cities were large and fortified, and the descendants of Anak were there.

medium.question: How did the spies’ report affect the Israelites?
answers: It discouraged them and weakened their courage
It made them rejoice
It caused them to go to war immediately
medium.explanation: The people said that their brothers had discouraged them and weakened their hearts.

medium.question: What was the connection between refusing to go up and the Israelites’ complaints?
answers: They refused because they did not know the way
They refused and complained that the Lord had brought them out to destroy them
They refused because they wanted to build cities in Egypt
medium.explanation: They first refused to go up and then complained that the Lord had brought them out of Egypt to hand them over to the Amorites.

medium.question: What does “you murmured in your tents” mean?
answers: You complained and grumbled
You rested and slept
You prepared for the journey
medium.explanation: The context shows that the Israelites spoke bitterly about the Lord and the land, so the phrase means that they complained.

challenge.question: What inner reason caused the Israelites to refuse to go up?
answers: They believed the land was empty of people
They feared the enemies and the size of the cities
They wanted to remain in the wilderness forever
challenge.explanation: They feared the large, tall people, the fortified cities, and the descendants of Anak, so their courage failed.

challenge.question: Which statement shows the Israelites’ most negative view of the Exodus?
answers: They said the Lord brought them out of Egypt to destroy them
They said the journey to the land was long
They said the cities in the land were small
challenge.explanation: They interpreted the Exodus not as salvation, but as a plan to hand them over to the Amorites and destroy them.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “cities great and walled up to heaven”?
answers: The cities were literally in heaven
The cities were abandoned
The expression emphasizes the strength of the fortifications and their fear
challenge.explanation: “To heaven” is an exaggerated expression emphasizing how high and strong the cities seemed to them.

questions.question: What inner reason caused the Israelites to refuse to go up?
answers: They believed the land was empty of people
They feared the enemies and the size of the cities
They wanted to remain in the wilderness forever
questions.explanation: They feared the large, tall people, the fortified cities, and the descendants of Anak, so their courage failed.

questions.question: Which statement shows the Israelites’ most negative view of the Exodus?
answers: They said the Lord brought them out of Egypt to destroy them
They said the journey to the land was long
They said the cities in the land were small
questions.explanation: They interpreted the Exodus not as salvation, but as a plan to hand them over to the Amorites and destroy them.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “cities great and walled up to heaven”?
answers: The cities were literally in heaven
The cities were abandoned
The expression emphasizes the strength of the fortifications and their fear
questions.explanation: “To heaven” is an exaggerated expression emphasizing how high and strong the cities seemed to them.

paragraphs.title: Moses Encourages the People to Trust the Lord

easy.question: What did Moses tell the Israelites not to fear?
answers: The enemies
The wilderness
Hunger
easy.explanation: Moses told them not to dread or fear the enemies.

easy.question: Who goes before the Israelites?
answers: Moses
The Lord their God
The angels
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Lord your God goes before you.”

easy.question: Where did Moses say that the Lord had already helped Israel?
answers: In the wilderness
In Canaan
In Egypt
easy.explanation: Moses recalled what the Lord had done for them in Egypt.

medium.question: Why did the Israelites not need to fear their enemies?
answers: The Lord would fight for them
The enemies were weak
Moses would hide them
medium.explanation: The Lord went before them and would fight for them.

medium.question: What order of actions is described in the verse?
answers: Israel fights, the Lord follows, and then they return to Egypt
The Lord goes before Israel and fights for them, as He did in Egypt
Moses fights, the Lord saves Egypt, and Israel remains in the wilderness
medium.explanation: First the Lord goes before the people, then fights for them, as He did in Egypt.

medium.question: What does “dread not” mean in this context?
answers: Run away
Praise
Be very afraid
medium.explanation: The phrase means to be very afraid or terrified; together with “neither be afraid,” it warns them not to fear the enemies.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “the Lord your God goes before you”?
answers: The Lord leads and directs Israel on the way
The Lord walks behind Israel
The Lord is unrelated to the journey
challenge.explanation: The phrase presents the Lord as leading the people and protecting them on the journey.

challenge.question: What does “before your eyes” emphasize about the Exodus?
answers: The events happened secretly
The Israelites themselves witnessed the Lord’s deeds
Only Moses heard about them
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the Israelites personally witnessed the Lord’s deeds in Egypt.

challenge.question: Why did Moses recall what the Lord had done in Egypt?
answers: To tell Israel to return to Egypt
To describe Egyptian life
To strengthen their confidence that the Lord would help them now
challenge.explanation: The reminder of the Lord’s miracles and help showed that He could fight for Israel again.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “the Lord your God goes before you”?
answers: The Lord leads and directs Israel on the way
The Lord walks behind Israel
The Lord is unrelated to the journey
questions.explanation: The phrase presents the Lord as leading the people and protecting them on the journey.

questions.question: What does “before your eyes” emphasize about the Exodus?
answers: The events happened secretly
The Israelites themselves witnessed the Lord’s deeds
Only Moses heard about them
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the Israelites personally witnessed the Lord’s deeds in Egypt.

questions.question: Why did Moses recall what the Lord had done in Egypt?
answers: To tell Israel to return to Egypt
To describe Egyptian life
To strengthen their confidence that the Lord would help them now
questions.explanation: The reminder of the Lord’s miracles and help showed that He could fight for Israel again.

paragraphs.title: The Lord Carries and Leads Israel in the Wilderness

easy.question: How is the Lord’s care for the people in the wilderness described?
answers: Like a father carrying his son
Like a king punishing his people
Like a teacher instructing students
easy.explanation: The verse compares the Lord’s care to a man carrying his son.

easy.question: In whom did the Israelites fail to believe?
answers: Moses
The Lord their God
The land of Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse says, “You did not believe the Lord your God.”

easy.question: What did the Lord do before the people on the way?
answers: Built houses for them
Gave them food
Went before them
easy.explanation: The verse describes the Lord as going before the people.

medium.question: Why did the Lord go before the Israelites on the way?
answers: To search out a place for them to camp
To punish their enemies
To return them to Egypt
medium.explanation: The verse says that He went before them to search out a place for them to pitch their tents.

medium.question: What does “to search out” mean in “to search out a place to pitch your tents”?
answers: To guard the place
To look for and inspect
To leave the place
medium.explanation: The phrase means to look for or investigate a suitable place for their camp.

medium.question: What sequence is described in these verses?
answers: The people reached the wilderness, and then the Lord began leading them
The Lord carried and led the people until they reached that place
The people camped and then asked the Lord to show them the way
medium.explanation: The verses first describe the Lord carrying and leading the people, and finally their arrival at the place where they were.

challenge.question: What is the central contrast in these verses?
answers: The Lord cared for and led the people, but the people did not believe Him
The people cared for the Lord, but He did not help them
The Lord did not lead the people, but they found the way
challenge.explanation: The verses describe the Lord’s guidance and care while also stating that the Israelites did not believe Him.

challenge.question: What can be learned from the fire at night and the cloud by day?
answers: The people traveled only at night
The Lord guided the people at all times
The people were afraid to travel in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: The fire at night and the cloud by day show that the Lord’s guidance continued day and night.

challenge.question: Why does the image “as a man carries his son” strengthen the message?
answers: It emphasizes military power
It emphasizes distance between the Lord and the people
It emphasizes closeness, care, and protection
challenge.explanation: Carrying a son expresses a close relationship and care, emphasizing the Lord’s protection of the people.

questions.question: What is the central contrast in these verses?
answers: The Lord cared for and led the people, but the people did not believe Him
The people cared for the Lord, but He did not help them
The Lord did not lead the people, but they found the way
questions.explanation: The verses describe the Lord’s guidance and care while also stating that the Israelites did not believe Him.

questions.question: What can be learned from the fire at night and the cloud by day?
answers: The people traveled only at night
The Lord guided the people at all times
The people were afraid to travel in the wilderness
questions.explanation: The fire at night and the cloud by day show that the Lord’s guidance continued day and night.

questions.question: Why does the image “as a man carries his son” strengthen the message?
answers: It emphasizes military power
It emphasizes distance between the Lord and the people
It emphasizes closeness, care, and protection
questions.explanation: Carrying a son expresses a close relationship and care, emphasizing the Lord’s protection of the people.

paragraphs.title: Unbelief and the Judgment on the Generation

easy.question: What did the Lord do after hearing the people’s words?
answers: He became angry and swore an oath
He praised them
He sent them to Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord heard their words, became angry, and swore an oath.

easy.question: Who was the one man from the evil generation whom the Lord said would see the land?
answers: Moses son of Amram
Caleb son of Jephunneh
Joshua son of Nun
easy.explanation: The verse specifically names Caleb son of Jephunneh as the exception.

easy.question: How is the land that the Lord swore to give the patriarchs described?
answers: A distant land
A difficult land
The good land
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly calls it “that good land.”

medium.question: What was the result of the evil generation’s sin?
answers: They would not see the land
They would receive another land
They would immediately return to Egypt
medium.explanation: The Lord swore that none of that evil generation would see the land promised to the patriarchs.

medium.question: What does “save Caleb” mean in this context?
answers: Before Caleb
Except for Caleb
After Caleb
medium.explanation: “Save” here means “except for”; Caleb was excluded from the judgment.

medium.question: Why did the Lord promise the land to Caleb?
answers: He was the first to leave Egypt
He was Moses’ son
He wholly followed the Lord
medium.explanation: The verse says that Caleb received the land because he wholly followed the Lord.

challenge.question: What does “he shall see it” refer to in verse 36?
answers: The good land that the Lord swore to give
The evil generation
The people’s words
challenge.explanation: The pronoun refers to the good land mentioned in the preceding verse.

challenge.question: What does “and to his children” show about the promise to Caleb?
answers: Only his children would enter the land
The promise also included his children
His children would remain in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the Lord would give the land to Caleb and his children, extending the promise to the next generation.

challenge.question: What is the central contrast between verses 35 and 36?
answers: Verse 35 discusses the wilderness and verse 36 Egypt
Verse 35 discusses Moses and verse 36 Aaron
Verse 35 denies the land to the evil generation, while verse 36 promises it to Caleb
challenge.explanation: Verse 35 describes the judgment on most of the generation, while verse 36 presents Caleb as the exception who receives the land.

answers: The good land that the Lord swore to give

questions.explanation: The pronoun refers to the good land mentioned in the preceding verse.

paragraphs.title: Joshua Will Lead Israel into the Land

easy.question: Who would enter the land and cause Israel to inherit it?
answers: Joshua son of Nun
Moses
Only the wilderness generation’s children
easy.explanation: The verse says that Joshua would go in and cause Israel to inherit the land.

easy.question: Why did Moses command the people to encourage Joshua?
answers: So he could lead them through the wilderness
Because Joshua would cause Israel to inherit the land
So he could build the tabernacle
easy.explanation: Joshua needed encouragement because he would lead Israel into its inheritance.

easy.question: Where did Moses command the people to turn and travel?
answers: To Jerusalem
To Mount Sinai
Into the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea
easy.explanation: Verse 40 says, “Turn and take your journey into the wilderness by the way of the Red sea.”

medium.question: What connection do the verses make between the people’s sins and Moses’ not entering the land?
answers: Because of the people, the Lord was angry with Moses too, so he would not enter
The people asked Moses not to enter
Moses chose to remain in the wilderness
medium.explanation: Moses says, “The Lord was angry with me for your sakes,” meaning that the people’s actions also provoked the Lord against him.

medium.question: Why would the younger Israelites enter the land?
answers: Because they were stronger
Because at that time they had no knowledge of good and evil
Because they already knew the land
medium.explanation: The verse says that the children, who at that time had no knowledge of good and evil, would enter and possess the land.

medium.question: What does “cause Israel to inherit it” mean?
answers: Guard it from a distance
Build a city there
Give it to Israel as an inheritance
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Joshua would lead Israel to receive the land as an inheritance.

challenge.question: What can be learned from the word “also” in “the Lord was angry with me also”?
answers: The Lord’s anger was directed at Moses as well as the people
Moses was also angry with Joshua
Moses would enter the land with the people
challenge.explanation: The word adds Moses to those judged: the Lord was angry with the people and with Moses.

challenge.question: What does “who stands before you” indicate about Joshua, in light of the rest of the verse?
answers: Joshua merely stood near Moses during the journey
Joshua was the leader prepared to continue Moses’ role
Joshua was not allowed to speak to the people
challenge.explanation: The phrase presents Joshua as the one prepared to lead, and the verse says he would cause Israel to inherit the land.

challenge.question: What sequence of events emerges from these verses?
answers: The children inherit the land, then Joshua is encouraged, and finally the people leave
The people enter the land, Moses returns to the wilderness, and Joshua is chosen
Moses does not enter, Joshua leads Israel, and the younger generation inherits the land
challenge.explanation: The verses present Moses’ exclusion, Joshua’s leadership, and the younger generation’s inheritance of the land.

answers: The Lord’s anger was directed at Moses as well as the people

questions.explanation: The word adds Moses to those judged: the Lord was angry with the people and with Moses.

questions.explanation: The phrase presents Joshua as the one prepared to lead, and the verse says he would cause Israel to inherit the land.

paragraphs.title: The People Try to Fight without a Command

easy.question: What did the Israelites admit at the beginning of verse 41?
answers: They had sinned against the Lord
They had conquered the mountain
Moses had sinned
easy.explanation: The Israelites said, “We have sinned against the Lord.”

easy.question: What did the Israelites do before going up the mountain?
answers: Built an altar
Put on their weapons of war
Asked Moses for forgiveness
easy.explanation: The verse says that each man girded on his weapons of war.

easy.question: What did the Lord command the Israelites to do?
answers: Go up and fight
Wait for Moses
Do not go up or fight
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “Go not up, neither fight.”

medium.question: Why did the Lord warn the Israelites not to go up and fight?
answers: They had no weapons
The Lord was not among them, and they could be defeated
Moses would not let them take food
medium.explanation: The Lord said He was not among them, so they could be defeated by their enemies.

medium.question: What does “you acted presumptuously” mean in this context?
answers: You acted defiantly and arrogantly
You fell asleep on the way
You succeeded in conquering
medium.explanation: The phrase means that they acted deliberately and rebelliously by going up despite the Lord’s warning.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events?
answers: The Lord warned them, they admitted their sin, and then they armed themselves
They went up, the Lord commanded them to go up, and then they admitted their sin
They admitted their sin, armed themselves, received the warning, and went up anyway
medium.explanation: They first admitted their sin and armed themselves; the Lord then warned them, but they went up anyway.

challenge.question: What contradiction stands out in the Israelites’ behavior?
answers: They admitted that they had sinned but then refused to obey
They feared war but took no weapons
They wanted to remain in the wilderness but asked for water
challenge.explanation: Although they admitted their sin, they rebelled against the Lord’s command and went up the mountain.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “I am not among you”?
answers: The Lord did not know where they were
They could not rely on the Lord’s help in battle
The Lord wanted them to fight alone so they could win
challenge.explanation: The phrase explains the warning: without the Lord’s presence and help, they would be defeated.

challenge.question: What does the movement from “you answered” to “you rebelled” and “acted presumptuously” show?
answers: They changed their minds and decided to obey
They completely forgot Moses’ words
Their response began as an admission but became deliberate rebellion
challenge.explanation: They first acknowledged their sin, but then refused to listen and acted defiantly.

questions.explanation: They first acknowledged their sin, but then refused to listen and acted defiantly.

paragraphs.title: Defeat, Weeping, and Staying at Kadesh

easy.question: What did the Amorites who lived in the mountain do?
answers: They chased the Israelites
They wept before the Lord
They stayed at Kadesh
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Amorites came out against the Israelites and chased them.

easy.question: What did the Israelites do after being chased and defeated?
answers: They began another battle
They returned and wept before the Lord
They immediately went to Hormah
easy.explanation: The verse says, “You returned and wept before the Lord.”

easy.question: Where did the Israelites stay for many days?
answers: In the mountain
At Seir
At Kadesh
easy.explanation: The final verse says, “You stayed at Kadesh many days.”

medium.question: What was the connection between the Israelites’ weeping and their staying at Kadesh?
answers: After the Lord would not listen to them, they remained at Kadesh for many days
They wept because they had already left Kadesh
They stayed at Kadesh in order to begin another battle
medium.explanation: They first wept before the Lord; after He did not listen, they remained at Kadesh for many days.

medium.question: What does “hearken” mean in “the Lord would not hearken to your voice”?
answers: Follow you
Listen and respond
Punish you
medium.explanation: “Hearken” means to listen attentively; the context says that the Lord did not listen to their plea or answer it.

medium.question: Why are the Amorites compared to bees?
answers: To say that the Amorites were small
To describe the battlefield
To emphasize their persistent pursuit and attack
medium.explanation: The comparison to bees emphasizes the intensity and persistence of the Amorites’ pursuit.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by “the Lord would not hearken to your voice, nor give ear unto you”?
answers: The Lord did not accept their request or respond to them
The Lord was not present there
The Lord did not know about the battle
challenge.explanation: The two parallel expressions emphasize that the Lord did not accept their cry or respond to it.

challenge.question: What can be understood from “in Seir, even unto Hormah”?
answers: The battle took place only inside Kadesh
They were defeated in the region of Seir, and the pursuit continued to Hormah
The Amorites fled from Hormah to Seir
challenge.explanation: The verse describes the place where they were defeated and the extent of the pursuit—from Seir to Hormah.

challenge.question: What does “according unto the days that ye abode there” emphasize at the end?
answers: The Israelites stayed at Kadesh for only one night
They immediately resumed their journey
Their stay at Kadesh was prolonged, like an earlier stay there
challenge.explanation: The comparison emphasizes that their stay at Kadesh lasted a long time, like their previous stay there.
